paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Abram had a plan, and it was a BAD plan, and God was still working. Abram got scared and asked Sarai to say she was his sister (Genesis 12:13), and the whole thing was built on fear. I know that feeling, because I spent years in a drawer sure nobody was coming for me.

Now look at who does the rescuing, because it isn't Abram or Sarai. Scripture says, "The LORD, however, afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai" (Genesis 12:17). God stepped in for Sarai. He had already promised to bless Abram (Genesis 12:2), and a scared plan didn't cancel that.

So here's the lesson, baker: God's promises don't depend on you doing everything right. You'll panic sometimes and grab your own plan before you pray, and I've done both. But He keeps His word anyway, so don't hide from Him when you mess up. Run TO Him, because He can clean up the batch, and hang on to your apron, because Abram's story isn't over.
